newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac in China visit to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac in China visit to boost ties.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac arrives in China on Thursday, bringing with him a huge delegation of business leaders, for a four-day state visit to boost political ties and win millions of dollars of business.

Some 60 heads of major French companies are accompanying Chirac on his trip, which will include meetings with China's top leaders in Beijing and the opening of a French technology exhibition grouping some 300 French firms in the booming commercial hub of Shanghai, officials said.

On the first day of his visit, Chirac will tell China's economic tsars of his ambitions to see China become one of France's major business partners and his hope that France will play a major role in the development and modernisation of China, French officials said before his departure.
Business sources have said the visit could see the signing of deals worth as much as $1.5 billion.
The Chinese side characterised ties as containing huge possibilities for further opening because "there exists a strong complementarity in both the economic and business sectors".

China regarded Chirac's takeover of power in 1995 as "the turning of a page" that had set bilateral relations on a healthy road, said Lu Yonghua, director general of the Commission for Economic Restructuring.

In terms of improved relations, officials cited the stand of Paris on Taiwan, which Beijing regards as a rebel province, and its decision to adopt a policy of dialogue rather than confrontation over human rights.

Sino-French relations soured in the early 1990s over sales of French jet fighters and frigates to China's rival, Taiwan, but have recovered since Paris pledged in 1994 to end arms sales to the island which Beijing considers a rebel province.
"The visit of President Chirac to China will bring substantive results in the areas of economics, politics and commerce," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang.
French sources expected the visit to set the seal on the Chinese purchase of 30 Airbus A320 airliners first announced in an April 1996 visit to France by Chinese Premier Li Peng.

Negotiations were under way on the sale of more Airbus planes to China -- possibly up to 100 -- but even on the eve of Chirac's arrival Airbus Industries officials refused to set a figure on the size of the planned deal.

Airbus holds a 15 percent market share in China, compared with about 40 percent in the rest of the world. China plans to buy about 2,000 civilian airliners during its current five-year plan that ends in 2000, and Chinese aviation officials have said they plan to boost the Airbus share of the market.

During Chirac's visit an "intermediate document" on a joint venture between Aviation Industries of China (AVIC), Singapore and a consortium involving Airbus to build a 100-seater airliner for assembly in China was expected to be signed, said sources close to the official delegation.
Also under discussion will be deals involving cereals, cement, thermal generators and clean coal as well as nuclear cooperation and financial services, officials said.

In addition, a senior official of insurer AXA-UAP, Jacques Friedman, a personal friend of Chirac, was expected to be in the delegation and industry sources said some form of deal on entering China's closely guarded insurance market was expected.
